cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Caches exist at every layer: browser and mobile app per user; DNS and CDN at the edge; reverse proxy or API gateway in front of the app; in-process memory or Redis in the app tier; and the database buffer pool.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: The closer a cache is to the user, the more a hit saves but the harder it is to invalidate. A private cache serves one user; a shared cache serves many and must never store private responses under shared keys. A near cache combines in-process L1 with shared Redis.

questions.q: Is a read replica a cache?
questions.a: Not exactly. It holds all data and answers any query via replication; a cache holds a subset for key lookups. Both can be stale.
Caching not-found results briefly so repeated lookups for missing keys do not reach the database.

questions.q: Why did MySQL remove its query cache?
questions.a: Any table write invalidated all its cached queries and a global lock serialized access.
